original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Kappa-blocker KB5b (explicit open request): residue class (i) of open problem F-star of research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7 (cert(M) >= floor(2v/3) for exact 3-total rational decoders), the tied-minimum / isotropic lines named as the exact residue by PR 2717. Three parts: (P1) PROVEN Lemma MX, a mixed anchor-repair-pivot certificate in two order forms with exact hypotheses, strictly subsuming Lemma AN (count of odd diagonals) and Lemma MP (matched-pivot certificate) as sufficient conditions; (P2) an exact per-line residue classification (anchor_good / repairable_1s / tied_isotropic) on PR 2111's stored fixtures tied_min (v = 12) and cex_min_1 (v = 19), with exhaustive maxima over all 4096 / 6144 pivot maps and replayed witnesses, plus the exact obstruction record for the mixed route on cex_min_1; (P3) a smallest-first bounded falsifier search in the tied domain (40 instances, v = 3..12, two tied-minimum generators), falsifier criterion an explicit admissible pairing B with sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j,A_j] < floor(2v/3) via the proven chain.

existing_restriction_being_changed: Nothing is relaxed. The restriction being addressed is PR 2717's stated demotion: Lemma AN handles only the even-diagonal count, not the repair or ordering of the tied-minimum (isotropic) lines. Every new claim carries its exact hypothesis and is demoted where unproved; no 'exactly when' or necessity wording is used.
method: Exact stdlib integer/F2 arithmetic. Engine adapted from PR 2717: for fixed a-labels the (b-labels, order, kept set) completion is exact by subset DP; a deterministic hill-climb over a-labels with exact completion; an independent witness checker replays every stored/constructed witness (supports, K_tt = 1, before-pair constraints recomputed from scratch). New: the per-line residue classification relative to the stored primitive 2-integral normalization; the Lemma MX construction (anchor labels on A, one-sided repairs on U, matched pivots on T, two block orders A+U-first and T-first) with per-map exact evaluation and replayed witnesses; exhaustive pivot-map maximization where the product of |D(t)| allows (4096 maps on tied_min, 6144 on cex_min_1); exact cert by exhaustive a-enumeration where the product of option counts is small; a bounded admissible-B scan (exhaustive at up to 12 free pairs, deterministic local search otherwise) as the rigorous falsifier criterion.
parameter_ranges: T = 3 totals exactly; rational decoders with nonzero diagonal. Fixtures: PR 2111's tied_min (v = 12, entries in {-1,0,1}) and cex_min_1 (v = 19, entries in {-1,0,1}), byte-identical data copies with recorded sha256. Search: v = 3..12, two instances per family and v, families tied_isotropic (every line constructed with exactly two tied minimal valuations at level 0 and even diagonal, entries in {+-1,+-2}) and mixed (half the lines unique-minimum with odd diagonal, half tied); 40 instances total.
nearest_overlapping_prs: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717 (Aaron Wang: Lemmas SF/MP/RK/AN and the exact residue statement; this package attacks the residue itself with a proved mixed lemma, an exact obstruction and a tied-domain search, not another lemma inventory). https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2335 (Aaron Wang: the 196-instance falsifier census over v = 4..12, entries -2..2; that domain is not repeated). https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162 (DreamingOfClouds: the fixtures, their recorded certificate limits and the T = 3 reductions; cited, not restated). https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2379 (Aaron Wang: exact cost 12 of tied_min) and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2206 (Nick Petalas: exact cost 21 of cex_min_1) are cited as context and not recomputed.
optimistic_full_cost_budget: No kappa, supplier, word or moment budget is in play (missing-lemma work). The whole-construction price is the evidence itself: the Lemma MX proof is in the README and every computational claim is recomputed by verify.py in one bounded stdlib run (no third-party packages, no solver).
bottleneck_link: F-star is the named route to closing every open T = 3 window at once (research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7, consequence PROVEN given F-star). Residue class (i) is the heart of the stated obstruction; a proof of the bound on the tied lines, or an exact obstruction to the known constructions there, narrows or closes that route; a falsifier would redirect the T = 3 decoder route entirely.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exact falsifier (smallest falsifying instance first: an explicit admissible B with chain cost below floor(2v/3), or exact cert below threshold where exhaustive), or, absent one, at the declared tied domain with every instance witnessed at or above threshold and the exact obstruction of the mixed route recorded. One bounded pivot maximum (the U-to-T class demotion and the second block order are the single pivot); early kill with the exact obstruction recorded. Compute cap: one session, single-process stdlib Python; the registered verify command runs about 306 s, below the 600 s manifest cap.

falsification_test: Side A of the search is the falsifier test for F-star: an explicit admissible pairing B with cost(B) < floor(2v/3) refutes F-star on that instance (the chain cost >= cert(M) is proven). Side B witnesses are rejected by the independent checker if any K_tt = 1 fails or any before-pair constraint fails; corrupted copies of stored witnesses fail verification (checked 2/2).

evidence: RESIDUE CLASS (i) CLOSED ON THE CANONICAL TIED INSTANCES AND THE SEARCHED TIED DOMAIN; EXACT OBSTRUCTION TO MIXING RECORDED; F-STAR ITSELF NOT PROVED. PROVEN (written proof in README.md): Lemma MX, a mixed anchor-repair-pivot certificate in two order forms (A+U-first and T-first) with exact hypotheses (one-sided repairs on U; A->T separation in the first form; T->(A union U) separation in the second), giving cert(M) >= |A| + |U| + sum_i MAS(Z[C_i]); its U = T empty special case is Lemma AN and its A = U empty special case is Lemma MP, so it subsumes both as sufficient conditions. CHECKED by verify.py (stdlib, deterministic, ~306 s, certificate digest 439d75261e9a2b9e): controls pass (brute/engine agreement 3/3 at v = 3, diagonal cert = 3, corrupted-witness rejection 2/2, MX all-anchor = AN count, MP control 5 with replayed witness). Residue classification on PR 2111's fixtures: tied_min has 0 anchor_good, 0 repairable_1s, 12 tied_isotropic (the mod-2 anchor is vacuous: 0 of 12); cex_min_1 has 8 anchor_good, 0 repairable_1s, 11 tied_isotropic (AN gives 8 against floor(2v/3) = 12). Exhaustive over all pivot maps as unit masks (4096 on tied_min, 6144 on cex_min_1): Lemma MP certifies 9 >= 8 (tied_min) and 16 >= 12 and >= 13 (cex_min_1) with replayed witnesses, so F-star holds on both canonical tied instances by a structural certificate; Lemma MX maximized over both order forms and three class variants gives the same 9 and 16. Exact obstruction to the mixed route on cex_min_1: the A->T separation fails for 6144/6144 pivot maps in the A-first form and the T->(A union U) separation fails for 6144/6144 in the T-first form, so no anchor/pivot mixture adds anything there in either block order. Engine witnesses 11 and 18 reproduce PR 2111's recorded one-copy L8 maxima (their CP-SAT optimality is CHECKED (recorded), not re-verified here). Tied-domain falsifier search, smallest first (40 instances, v = 3..12, families tied_isotropic and mixed): zero falsifiers; cert = v on all 40 (16 decided by exhaustive a-enumeration at v <= 6, 24 pinned by full-size replayed witnesses); minimum witness ratio 1.0; the bounded admissible-B scan found no chain cost below floor(2v/3) on any instance; Lemma MP reaches v on all 40 and Lemma MX is never below MP and never strictly above it on this domain (mx_strictly_above_mp = 0). NOT PROVED: F-star for general rational decoders; that matched pivots always reach floor(2v/3) (witnessed on 42 instances, not proved); residue classes (ii) non-3-dichromatic zero digraphs and (iii) non-dyadic entries are untouched; the B-scan values are bounded-search upper bounds on the minimum chain cost, not exact minima; no hypothesis is claimed necessary.

open_questions.question: Is max_c sum_i MAS(Z[C_i]) >= floor(2v/3) for every rank-3 zero digraph Z with pivot maps c into D(t)? (Equivalently: does the matched-pivot family of Lemma MP always certify the F-star bound?)
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lemma MP would then prove F-star outright for all exact 3-total decoders; this package witnesses it (with cert = v) on all 42 tied-domain instances tested, including both canonical fixtures where the mod-2 anchor fails.
open_questions.first_step: Adversarially construct decoders minimizing max_c sum_i MAS(Z[C_i]), smallest v first, using the two-tied-minima generator with dense zero digraphs subject to Lemma RK's constraints (no mutual-zero K_4, no transitive 4-tournament, block incidences of size >= 2).
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing structural; needs a dedicated enumeration session.

open_questions.question: Does insertion-finite mixing help? (Allow each anchor line to be inserted at a valid cut of the pivot order instead of taking one of the two block orders.)
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two block orders fail completely on cex_min_1 (6144/6144 maps in both forms); the exact cut criterion (pivot-block out-neighbours all preceding in-neighbours in one linear extension) is the precise remaining power of the mixed route, and its failure would close naive mixing entirely.
open_questions.first_step: Implement the cut criterion and re-run on cex_min_1's 6144 pivot maps; record how many anchor lines become placeable and the resulting certified bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: None; small code extension of verify.py.

open_questions.why_it_matters: Those certificates exceed everything the anchor and matched-pivot families reach (9 and 16); classifying the extra label patterns (two-bit labels, off-pivot pairs) would name the labelling family a proof of residue class (i) actually needs.
